rows.description: A teenager is asked to eat separately or is not invited to a meal because of religion, caste or diet. Feeling less than others hurts deeply; adults should name exclusion as wrong and act to end it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Eating with friends of every kind [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult in a hostel or college shares meals across faiths, castes and diets and finds home rules and friendship rules clash. Respecting a friend's restrictions while questioning unfair purity ideas takes care.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult keeps a family's food custom at home yet offers guests a choice, and never mocks anyone's plate. Food traditions can be loved without becoming a wall against others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A mother keeps putting more roti on a plate and takes refusal as rejection. The observer sees that food is her language of love, and a kind response is to thank her and eat a little more or explain warmly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler at Diwali, Eid or Christmas reacts to lamps, sweets and crowds with wonder or fear of loud noise. The child absorbs the mood of the house even without knowing the meaning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, curiosity, awe

rows.description: A child helps make rangoli, decorate a tree or fly a kite, and is proud to have a real task. Festivals give children a place in the group and a calendar of things to look forward to.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child hears the tale behind Holi, Eid, Onam or Baisakhi and asks why. Stories give identity, and children often take home a sense of both their own festival and their friends' festivals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager is pulled into cleaning, cooking and visits while wanting friends or rest. Grumbling and real belonging sit together; some duty can be shared and some personal time asked for.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager from a minority or a migrant family sees neighbours celebrating and feels outside. Invitations from friends and neighbours make a large difference and cost very little.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student or worker far from home sees the lights on a screen and feels a sharp ache. Calling home, cooking one dish or joining a local group can ease it without pretending the loss is small.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
